stem: A test with 1 million users per variant shows conversion of 10.00% in control and 10.15% in treatment: +0.15 percentage points, or +1.5% relative, with p below 0.001. The change is costly to build and to maintain. What is the best advice?

options.text: Ship it: a p-value below 0.001 shows that the change really matters for the business
The effect is very likely real but small; ship only if +0.15 points pays back the cost
Do not trust it: with a lift this small, a p-value below 0.001 must come from a data error
Rerun it: a lift below 2% relative can never be statistically significant
